task: Add a read-only GET /v1/analytics/assistants-requests endpoint in codemie that returns one TabularResponse row per conversation_assistant_usage ES document, with the standard analytics filters plus assistant_id, paging, and the same authenticate + AccessFilter scoping as assistants-chats.

key_reasoning.reason: Three components over two layers: a new route in analytics/usage.py, a new AssistantHandler method on the AnalyticsQueryPipeline/ES|QL path, and AnalyticsService delegation. The AccessFilter and TabularResponse are reused, not changed.

Nearest patterns are assistants-chats (ES|QL + AccessFilter) and routing/sessions (row-level tabular analytics). They cover the auth and access scoping, so the security auto-bump does not apply. Two things are still open: (1) paging raw rows through ES|QL, which has no OFFSET and is capped at LIMIT 1000; (2) per-row exposure of user name and email to project admins. Both are design choices, not new territory.

About 6-8 files are modified and 0-1 are new: the usage.py route, assistant_handler.py, analytics_service.py, possibly a query-params/column model, the OpenAPI baseline (and possibly route_precedence) guard snapshots, and test_assistant_handler.py, test_analytics_service.py and test_analytics.py. These span the routers, service/analytics and tests trees.
API, Service and read-only Elasticsearch persistence along the standard path. No schema or index changes, and no changes to metric emission.
Fields, filters, auth model and out-of-scope items are all listed. The small open points are sort order, how paging works against the ES|QL cap, and how to treat request_id when it is null.
